name: DPF Cleaner

features.text: Removes soot and ash deposits from blocked filters.
Can restore power, fuel economy and extend service life.
Ideal for vehicles in limp mode or after a failed regeneration process.

description: A low-foam, non-flammable formula specifically designed to quickly and efficiently eliminate particulates, carbon and other deposits in dirty diesel particulate filters (DPF), without the need to dismantle or remove the filter.
application: Direction: 1) Check for fault codes and confirm particulate filter blockage. 2) Check engine oil level. 3) Confirm vehicle has as least a ¼ a tank of fuel before starting service. 4) Bring vehicle up to operating temperature and switch off engine. For Euro 6 diesel vehicles disconnect the Air Flow Sensor to prevent the low pressure EGR Valve from operating during the application process: 1) Remove the temperature sensor, oxygen sensor, or pressure sensor and feed the applicator tube directly into the opening towards the direction of the particulate filter. Ensure the chosen sensor is lower than the turbo to prevent product from running back into the engine. 2) Spray Cleaner into the particulate filter until the can is empty. 3) Allow the product to soak for 15-30 minutes. 4) Reattach the pressure sensor pipe, temperature or oxygen sensor. 5) If Air Flow Sensor was disconnected, reconnect. Restart engine and idle for 5 minutes. Then run the engine at 1500 - 2000 rpm for 5 minutes. 6) Test Drive vehicle for 10- 15 minutes. Clear any fault codes and reset particulate filter data, if required. 7) Initiate a forced regeneration of the diesel particulate filter using a diagnostic test via the OBD port and take the vehicle on a test drive. * *Refer to vehicle manufacturers’ instructions for code reset and forced regeneration procedures.

ad.headline: Remove Soot And Ash
ad.description:
A non-flammable formula specifically designed to quickly and efficiently eliminate particulates, carbon and other deposits in dirty diesel particulate filters (DPF), without the need to dismantle or remove the filter.

Diesel Particulate Filters (DPFs) are designed to trap and remove soot from diesel engine exhaust, helping to reduce emissions. However, certain driving habits can lead to excessive soot buildup, causing the filter to become clogged.
benefits: Removes soot and ash deposits from blocked filters.
Can restore power, fuel economy and extend service life.
No need to remove the particulate filter from the vehicle.
Faster and more cost-effective method than disassembly.
Ideal for vehicles in limp mode or after a failed regeneration process.
